The current task is a long-horizon engineering effort to add professional retouch/paint and surrounding workflows (starting with Clone Stamp) while preserving the existing tiled architecture, copy-on-write history, undo/redo, selection/mask/edit-target behavior, persistence, and cross-browser compatibility. Milestone 1 requires a Clone Stamp tool with explicit source/aligned-unaligned/coordinate model, selection clipping, mask/edit-target respect, atomic undoable transactions, persistence/recovery, missing-source safety, and focused unit plus browser tests, without regressing Brush/Eraser. Later milestones extend retouch/paint tools, selection/transform/adjustment/layer workflows, local-first partial-hydration persistence, rendering/format compatibility (including optional GPU fallback with CPU oracle), and professional shell hardening. The assistant began by inspecting the repository (directory listing, file tree, and key architecture/document/tool-registry files) to understand existing systems before implementing Milestone 1.

The raster-engine package exposes deterministic, sparse-aware painting and adjustment primitives that operate on PixelLayer, SelectionMask, RasterMask, and TiledCoverageStore. Stroke and mask-stroke functions interpolate brush points into dabs, compute local dab bounds from the inverse layer transform, read only the affected region, apply falloff/opacity/pressure/selection coverage, and return minimal PixelPatch or CoveragePatch with changed bounds. Selection coverage is sampled sparsely for isolated queries and densified only for the union of dab bounds. Brightness adjustment supports full-layer and selection-bounded modes, with a separate path that writes directly into an immutable TiledPixelStore one tile at a time. Layer/image resize resamples pixel stores, coverage stores, raster masks, and vector masks, validates transforms and sizes, and enforces a MAX_RESIZE_WORKING_BYTES working-set limit. adjustment layers own a typed Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, or Invert payload, with an optional canvas-sized document-space raster mask, and parameters and masks remain editable and never rewrite underlying pixel layers; renderable layers own an ordered list of validated color-overlay, outside-stroke, and drop-shadow effects, with effect enabled state, opacity, color, blend mode, size, offsets, and blur as canonical editable data, and source pixels and structured payloads are never baked when an effect changes.
